sec: Features: the alkalosis triad and ECF volume contraction · p825

items.q: The features triangle of metabolic alkalosis links alkalosis with which two other findings?
items.exp: The triangle is drawn as Alkalosis at the apex with Hypokalemia and HTN at the base. (Book p825)

items.q: A patient has an alkalosis together with hypokalemia and hypertension. Which group of causes does the triad point to?
opts: The saline-responsive ECF volume contraction group
Post-hypercapnic alkalosis after correction of chronic respiratory failure
items.exp: Hypokalemia with hypertension completes the triangle of alkalosis–hypokalemia–HTN, the pattern of saline-unresponsive mineralocorticoid excess. (Book p825)

items.q: Match the features of ECF volume contraction — 1) Secondary hyperreninemic hyperaldosteronism  2) ↓GFR  3) Overall label … A) Saline responsive alkalosis  B) Causes hypokalemia and alkalosis  C) ↓Urine Cl⁻ and ↓urine K⁺
items.exp: ECF volume contraction: secondary hyperreninemic hyperaldosteronism → hypokalemia and alkalosis; ↓GFR → ↓urine Cl⁻ and ↓urine K⁺; the whole picture is saline responsive alkalosis. (Book p825)

items.q: In ECF volume contraction, the fall in GFR is accompanied by which urinary changes?
items.exp: ↓GFR → ↓urine Cl⁻, ↓urine K⁺ in the ECF-volume-contraction pathway. (Book p825)

items.q: Match the causes of ECF volume contraction — 1) GI  2) Renal drug  3) Renal tubulopathy (Bartter)  4) Renal tubulopathy (Gitelman) … A) Diuretics  B) Vomiting / NG aspiration  C) Mg²⁺/K⁺ depletion with salt wasting at the TAL  D) Distal convoluted tubule dysfunction
items.exp: Causes of ECF volume contraction: GI — vomiting/NG aspiration; renal — diuretics, post hypercapnia, cystic fibrosis, Mg²⁺/K⁺ depletion, Bartter syndrome and Gitelman syndrome. (Book p825)

items.q: Which of these is listed as a renal cause of ECF-volume-contraction alkalosis?
items.exp: The renal column lists diuretics, post hypercapnia, cystic fibrosis, Mg²⁺/K⁺ depletion, Bartter syndrome and Gitelman syndrome. (Book p825)

items.q: All but one of the following are printed causes of ECF-volume-contraction (saline-responsive) alkalosis. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Conn's syndrome sits in the saline-*unresponsive* ECF volume expansion group; vomiting, NG aspiration, cystic fibrosis, diuretics, Bartter and Gitelman are the contraction causes. (Book p825)

items.q: ‘Alkalosis with hypokalemia but without hypertension favours the saline-responsive group of causes.’
opts: True — hypertension completes the mineralocorticoid-excess triangle
False — hypertension is not part of the triangle
False — saline-responsive alkalosis is always normotensive with hyperkalemia
True, but only if the urine chloride is > 40 mEq/L
items.exp: The triangle is alkalosis with hypokalemia *and* HTN; without hypertension the ECF-volume-contraction (saline-responsive) causes are more likely. (Book p825)
